memory_candidates.content: To build many git stash reflog entries fast in a test fixture (e.g. to reproduce a SIGPIPE on `git stash list | head -1`), use `git stash create "<distinct message>"` (same dirty tree, different message -> different commit SHA, no working-tree mutation per entry) plus `git update-ref --create-reflog -m "<msg>" refs/stash "$sha" "$old"`. Gotcha: `git update-ref` silently no-ops (appends no reflog line) when old==new SHA, so reusing a single stash SHA across iterations produces only one entry regardless of loop count -- each iteration needs a genuinely distinct commit object. ~2000 entries built this way in ~12s.

Bash command-substitution failure guard pattern for a script under `set -euo pipefail` with a mix of fatal and recoverable failure sites: `if ! VAR=$(cmd 2>&1); then echo "WARNING -- <reason>; git said: $VAR" >&2; VAR=""; fi` for a site with an independent backstop (continue, exit 0 overall), versus the same shape but `rm -f <tmp>; exit 1` for a site with no backstop. Capturing stderr via `2>&1` (not `2>/dev/null`) and echoing it verbatim in the warning/reason line lets a reader distinguish transient contention (e.g. a held .git/index.lock) from genuine damage, without changing the success-path stdout contract.
